open_points.subject: EXECUTION_STATUS_CONCLUSIONS
open_points.text: the conclusion each NodeExecution status gives (A13 rules 5 and 7)
open_points.question: What are the exact row and cell values of EXECUTION_STATUS_CONCLUSIONS, especially for outcome_unknown, whose conclusion changes when its EffectAttempt is resolved, and refused_by_owner, which ends the run refused rather than behaving like an ordinary failed node?
options: Map each status directly to a static conclusion member
Give outcome_unknown a member meaning consult the EffectAttempt and refused_by_owner a distinct conclusion
Exclude context-dependent statuses from this table despite the stated totality
open_points.default_guess: Use a total map to conclusion members including distinct consult_effect_attempt and refused conclusions.

open_points.subject: NODE_CONCLUSION_EFFECTS
open_points.text: what each node conclusion means for the run and for its dependants (A13 rules 5 and 7)
open_points.question: What is the closed node-conclusion enumeration, and what exact run effect and dependant effect does each member map to?
options: One table row with separate run-effect and dependant-effect cells
Two separate correspondences, one for run effects and one for dependant effects
One combined effect enumeration whose members encode both consequences
open_points.default_guess: Define a node-conclusion enumeration and a row with separate run-effect and dependant-effect members.

open_points.subject: data_provider table row and cell models
open_points.text: `models`: the row models of its tables and the enumerations their cells name.
open_points.question: Which row models and cell enumerations are added to models for EXECUTION_STATUS_CONCLUSIONS, NODE_CONCLUSION_EFFECTS, WAIT_REASON_RESTING_STATUSES and HTTP_METHOD_BODIES? State 1 defines only M01–M28 and does not define conclusion, node-effect or body-presence taxonomies.
options: Add explicit row models and new enumerations to models
Use existing enumerations where possible and booleans or tuples for the other cells
Treat the tables as untyped mappings despite saying their rows and cells are models members
open_points.default_guess: Add explicit row models and closed enumerations for every non-existing cell taxonomy.

open_points.subject: HTTP_METHOD_BODIES
open_points.text: whether an HTTP method carries a body (A09 rule 2) — is a correspondence over that taxonomy ... whose cells name members
open_points.question: What enumeration member represents carries-body versus no-body? A09 fixes the semantic mapping, but models defines no body-presence enumeration, and a Boolean cell would not “name members.”
options: Add a body-presence enumeration with body and no_body members
Use Boolean cells and relax “whose cells name members”
Use request-placement members such as query and body
open_points.default_guess: Add a request-body-presence enumeration and map GET/DELETE to no_body and POST/PUT/PATCH to body.

open_points.subject: ownership of A13 conclusion policy
open_points.text: `run_graph` ... Owns A13 rules 2, 4, 5, 7 and 8 as one derivation ... [while `data_provider` owns] the conclusion each NodeExecution status gives ... what each node conclusion means for the run and for its dependants ... the status a run rests in for each wait reason
open_points.question: Does data_provider now own the normative A13 mappings with run_graph only interpreting them, or does run_graph still own those rules and data_provider merely encode values supplied by run_graph?
options: Transfer ownership of the listed correspondences to data_provider
Keep rule ownership in run_graph and state that data_provider owns only their literal representation
Split ownership explicitly by naming the exact A13 clauses retained by run_graph
open_points.default_guess: Keep semantic rule ownership in run_graph and make data_provider the sole owner only of the typed literal tables implementing those rules.
